title: Family of man shot dead by B.C. Mounties want charges as inquest ends
article: The family of a man shot by Mounties in Kamloops, B.C., almost two years ago say they still have faith someone will be charged in his death.
The relatives spoke after testimony wrapped up at an inquest into the shooting of Wilbert Bartley, who was killed after he rammed his vehicle into an unmarked police van in July of 2010.
Officers from the Calgary Police Service who investigated the shooting found no wrongdoing on the part of the officers involved and did not recommend charges.
But Bartley's sister, Wanda Doubt, says the family promised Wilbert justice, and they want someone charged in what they believe was a wrongful death.
The inquest jury is not charged with finding fault or blame, but to make recommendations aimed at preventing similar tragedies in future.

The officers involved in the shooting testified they acted in self defence, while a toxicologist said Bartley had elevated levels of methamphetamine in his system when he died, as well as low levels of alcohol, cocaine and morphine. (CFJC)
